veranderings.voor: Stel jou voor mense kry ou goed in die Kaap se sand.
veranderings.na: Stel jou voor dat mense ou goed in die Kaap se sand kry.
veranderings.rede: Written Afrikaans links 'stel jou voor' to its clause with 'dat' and verb-final order; the spoken run-on reads loosely.

veranderings.voor: wat sandbanke en rotse net onder die water wys.
veranderings.na: wat sandbanke en rotse wys wat net onder die water lê.
veranderings.rede: As written 'net' can be read as 'only' (shows them only under water); placing it with 'lê' makes it clearly 'just below the surface'.

veranderings.blok: Kies wat by die vraag pas
veranderings.na: Van die leidrade wat wel by die vraag pas,
veranderings.rede: 'wat pas' hangs without saying what they fit; the heading's own phrase makes the contrast with the set-aside letter clear.

veranderings.blok: Kies wat by die vraag pas
veranderings.voor: want hulle is op daardie plek gevind
veranderings.na: want die stukke is op daardie plek gevind
veranderings.rede: 'hulle' sits right after 'die matrose se briewe' and can be read as referring to the letters; naming the pieces removes the ambiguity.

veranderings.voor: wat los van mekaar begin en tog
veranderings.na: wat los van mekaar ontstaan en tog
veranderings.rede: Sources do not 'begin'; 'ontstaan' is the natural verb for where a clue comes from independently.

veranderings.voor: want 'n nuwe leidraad kan hom verander.
veranderings.na: want 'n nuwe leidraad kan dit verander.
veranderings.rede: 'dit' is the standard written pronoun for an abstract noun like 'gevolgtrekking' and matches the glossary entry, which already says 'kan dit verander'.

beskerm_bedenkings.rede: Asked explicitly: I think it is acceptable Afrikaans for a nine-year-old. It is a regular, transparent noun-plus-noun compound built like 'inligtingsbron' or 'kragbron', needs no linking -s, and both parts are words a Grade 4 learner knows, so its meaning can be read off the word itself. It is probably not in a dictionary, but Afrikaans forms compounds freely and that does not make it wrong. I propose no change; if a different form is ever chosen it must go through all three lessons and the agreed-wordings list, as the entry says.
